title: Deterministic interleaving scheduler with tenant-weighted fairness
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: Design and implement a deterministic interleaving scheduler that enforces tenant-weighted fairness across prefill and decode phases while allowing kernel-selection hints and attention-window awareness. Goal is to reduce SLA jitter (95th/99th latency tails) for tenants with reserved SLAs while preserving overall throughput for best-effort traffic.
acceptance_criteria: New scheduler can be enabled behind a feature flag per-pool
95th percentile tail latency improves by >=10% for reserved-tenant workload in our synthetic SLAs benchmark compared to the baseline fairband scheduler
Throughput (tokens/sec) for mixed workloads degrades by <=5% under typical production load
Scheduler emits per-request decision trace with phase assignment, kernel_hint, and tenant_weight buckets
Automated A/B canary rollout completes with health checks and rollback on regressions
proposed_solution: Introduce a deterministic time-slice interleaver that slices work at phase boundaries (prefill vs decode) and assigns micro-slices to tenants according to a configurable weight vector. Use kernel_selection hints (e.g., low-latency kernel preferred) at micro-slice granularity to co-locate compatible work. Add attention-window estimation pass to avoid slicing in the middle of large KV-cache-prefetch prefetch windows. Provide soft-degradation policy where best-effort tenants are opportunistically throttled when headroom is needed for reserved tenants.
decisions: Use deterministic round-robin with weight buckets rather than purely opportunistic hedging to improve reproducibility of tail latencies
Phase splitting will be aligned to KV-cache boundaries to avoid costly re-priming; small phases (<8 tokens) may be coalesced
Kernel hints will be advisory: scheduler tries to pack same-kernel slices together but will fall back based on deadline pressure
Expose tenant weights as runtime-configurable via console and API for Dedicated customers
comments: 2026-03-05 - Aisha: Initial RFC posted. Outlined deterministic interleaver + tenant weights. Asked for benchmark suggestions and constraints for Dedicated customers.

2026-03-06 - Marco: Ran microbenchmarks on r5g and a100 testbeds. Deterministic interleaving reduces 95p jitter in toy workload by ~12% when weights are 4:1 reserved:best-effort. Noted throughput drop ~6% with aggressive kernel packing; suggests kernel_hint as advisory.
2026-03-08 - Design review (Priya): UX for runtime weight controls should allow per-customer presets (SLA, best-effort, burst). Requested a simple fallback UI and a link to console rollout plan.

2026-03-09 - Eng: Implemented prototype scheduler in staging runtime. Added tracepoint tags: slice_id, phase, tenant_bucket, kernel_hint. Found edge case where long prefill for very long prompts caused starvation of small decode-only requests; created follow-up ENG-438218.

2026-03-11 - QA: Synthetic SLA benchmarks run across 4 pools. 95p latency improved between 10-18% for reserved tenants. 99p tail shows mixed results (some outliers remain); hypothesis is occasional kernel-selection miscoordination causing re-priming costs.
2026-03-12 - Marco: Added mitigation for kernel-mismatch by allowing fast-path hedged reassignments when deadline < 20ms. Re-ran tests; 99p improved modestly, throughput impact negligible.
2026-03-12 - PM (Lena): Confirmed priority for this feature due to upcoming Dedicated customer pilot. Requested docs and runbook for canary rollout.
2026-03-12 - Security: No direct data plane changes; security review flagged need to ensure trace ids do not leak PII. Added to rollout checklist.
metrics_target: 95p-latency: -10% reserved tenant; throughput: <=5% regression; error-rate: no increase
rollout_plan: Feature flag gate per-cluster and per-pool
Canary 2 pools (internal) at 5% traffic for 48h with synthetic SLA checks
Expand to Dedicated pilot customers (manual opt-in) for 7 days
If stable, enable gradual ramp to 50% over 2 weeks; monitor 95p/99p, kernel-mismatch counters, and cost impact
Full enable with default weights only after sign-off from performance and SRE
risks_mitigation: Risk: Kernel-mismatch increases re-priming latency. Mitigation: advisory kernel_hint packing + hedged reassign when small deadline remains
Risk: Starvation of tiny decode-only requests. Mitigation: minimum reserved micro-slice per-cycle and preemption window for tail latency requests
Risk: Operator misconfiguration of tenant weights. Mitigation: safe defaults and console warnings with estimated impact preview
